purpose: machine-facing knowledge base of concrete physical-computing and automation work units (IoT/home automation, automation logic, robotics basics, electrical and fail-safe safety) for planning, sequencing, risk control, and validated execution; a subdomain node of Hardware, Microcontrollers & Self-Hosting within a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence is supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the maker's goal is to 'automate things' in a home/hobby-to-prosumer context, not industrial-grade certified automation
key references are Banzi & Shiloh (Getting Started with Arduino) and Upton & Halfacree (Raspberry Pi User Guide)
nodes are concrete physical-computing/automation work units bounded to one heavy reasoning session
closed-loop sensor->actuator work explicitly ties to the feedback-loops specialist
exclusions: PCB/silicon design and custom IC layout
industrial PLC certification and functional-safety SIL processes
deep control-theory proofs and full SLAM/path planning
cloud backend/web application development beyond device connectivity
general software engineering unrelated to firmware or automation

competency_questions.question: What does the project need to sense, decide, and actuate, and within what budget?
Should this run on a microcontroller, a single-board computer, or a hub, and why?
What electrical, fusing, and enclosure measures keep the build safe in its environment?
How are the platform, firmware, sensors, and connectivity made to coexist without blocking?
How are sensors read and actuators driven reliably at the hardware level?
How is sensed state turned into coordinated, predictable actuator action?
How do devices connect, message, update, and stay secure over the network?
How does the hub model device state so cross-device automations are coherent?
What guarantees the system reaches a safe state on any fault, hang, or sensor loss?
How is automation behavior made observable and debuggable without physical access?
How is closed-loop and safety behavior validated before it controls real hardware?
How is the system deployed, commissioned, and maintained over its lifecycle?

glossary.definition: separated/safety extra-low voltage; a bounded low-voltage domain isolated from mains.
a control structure where a sensor reading drives an actuator toward a setpoint.
the property that faults drive the system to a defined non-harmful state.
a device that converts a control signal into physical action (relay, motor, solenoid, servo).
a lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol for device state and commands.
a timer that resets or safe-states the device if firmware fails to service it.
a deadband around a setpoint that prevents an on/off controller from chattering.
over-the-air firmware update delivered over the network with versioning and rollback.

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; all values are heuristic priors referencing SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR.

source_registry.description: model heuristic priors for physical computing and automation work units, drawing on standard maker references (Banzi & Shiloh, Getting Started with Arduino; Upton & Halfacree, Raspberry Pi User Guide).

nodes.definition: Define what the physical-computing/automation project must sense, actuate, and decide before any wiring or code.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: user adds a new automation trigger or operating environment

pros.claim: scope clarity prevents rework
pros.example: writing 'turn on fan when temp>28C and humidity>60%' fixes sensor+actuator+rule choices at once

cons.claim: over-scoping stalls a hobby build
cons.example: specifying industrial PLC redundancy for a single houseplant waterer

failure_modes: vague goal yields wrong sensor selection
missing environment spec causes outdoor enclosure failure
acceptance_tests: requirement set lists every sense/decide/act triple with measurable thresholds
each requirement has an acceptance threshold

nodes.definition: Specify voltage/current budgets, fusing, isolation, and mains-vs-low-voltage boundaries so the build cannot start a fire or shock anyone.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any load above SELV limits or a new mains-switching element is introduced

pros.claim: correct fusing limits fault energy
pros.example: a 1A fuse on a 5V sensor rail prevents a shorted wire from melting insulation

cons.claim: safety work feels invisible until it fails catastrophically
cons.example: skipping isolation on a relay switching mains can backfeed the logic board

failure_modes: missing isolation lets mains reach low-voltage logic
acceptance_tests: every mains path is fused and isolated from SELV logic
calculated fault current is below conductor and connector ratings
ground/bond continuity verified

nodes.definition: Choose microcontroller (Arduino-class) vs single-board computer (Raspberry Pi-class) vs hybrid based on real-time, I/O, compute, and power needs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new latency, compute, or connectivity requirement crosses the chosen platform's limits

pros.claim: matching platform to timing needs avoids redesign
pros.example: hard-real-time PWM motor control belongs on an MCU, not a non-RT Linux SBC

cons.claim: premature platform lock blocks scaling
cons.example: choosing an 8-bit MCU then needing TLS networking forces a rewrite

failure_modes: SBC chosen where deterministic timing required
MCU chosen where heavy compute/networking needed

nodes.definition: Wire and read sensors (analog, digital, I2C/SPI/1-Wire) with correct levels, pull-ups, and calibration to produce trustworthy measurements.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new sensor type/bus is introduced or readings drift beyond calibration tolerance

pros.claim: calibration turns raw counts into usable physical values
pros.example: two-point calibration maps a thermistor's ADC counts to degrees C

cons.claim: noisy/uncalibrated reads corrupt every downstream rule
cons.example: an un-debounced reed switch triggers false motion events

failure_modes: missing pull-up floats an I2C bus

nodes.definition: Drive actuators (relays, solenoids, DC/stepper/servo motors) through proper drivers with flyback/snubber protection and current limits.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new actuator or higher-current load is wired to a driver

pros.claim: a flyback diode protects the driver from inductive kickback
pros.example: a relay coil's collapse spike is clamped instead of frying the transistor

cons.claim: inductive loads destroy unprotected drivers silently
cons.example: a solenoid without a snubber degrades a MOSFET over weeks until failure

failure_modes: GPIO driving inductive load directly fails
acceptance_tests: every inductive load has flyback/snubber protection
peak/stall current is within driver and supply ratings
drive signals validated under load

nodes.definition: Use motor controllers and basic kinematics (wheel/joint geometry, speed/position) to turn motion intent into coordinated actuator commands.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the mechanism geometry or a motion-accuracy requirement changes

pros.claim: simple kinematics make motion predictable
pros.example: differential-drive equations turn a target heading into left/right wheel speeds

cons.claim: ignoring kinematics yields drift and unrepeatable motion
cons.example: open-loop wheel timing accumulates heading error over distance

nodes.definition: Establish device network/radio links (WiFi, BLE, optionally LoRa/Zigbee) with provisioning, reconnection, and link-loss handling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the network topology, credentials, or radio protocol changes

pros.claim: robust reconnection keeps automations alive
pros.example: exponential backoff reconnect recovers a sensor node after a router reboot

cons.claim: naive connectivity drops events during outages
cons.example: a device that blocks forever on WiFi connect stops reading its sensors

nodes.definition: Design MQTT topic structure, QoS, retain, and last-will so devices and the hub exchange state and commands reliably.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the device fleet, broker, or topic taxonomy changes

pros.claim: structured topics + retain give late subscribers current state
pros.example: home/livingroom/temp retained lets a dashboard show last value on reconnect

cons.claim: flat topic spaces and wrong QoS lose or duplicate commands
cons.example: QoS0 actuator commands silently drop when a device briefly disconnects

nodes.definition: Integrate devices into a hub (e.g. Home Assistant) defining entities, areas, and discovery so automations have one coherent state model.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new device class is integrated or the hub model is restructured

pros.claim: a hub centralizes state for cross-device automations
pros.example: Home Assistant exposes a motion sensor and a light as entities a single rule can link

cons.claim: hub lock-in and config sprawl complicate migration
cons.example: hundreds of YAML automations become hard to audit or port off the hub

nodes.definition: Author automation logic: triggers, conditions, actions, and schedules that map sensed state to actuator actions deterministically.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new trigger, actuator, or scheduling requirement is added to the rule set

pros.claim: explicit triggers+conditions make behavior predictable
pros.example: 'if motion and after-sunset then lights on for 5 min' is auditable and testable

cons.claim: rule interactions create emergent, hard-to-debug behavior
cons.example: two rules toggling the same light race and flicker it

failure_modes: missing condition fires at wrong time

nodes.definition: Close the loop from sensor to actuator (on/off hysteresis, PID) with stability, anti-windup, and bounded response; ties to the feedback-loops specialist.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the controlled plant dynamics, setpoint, or sensor latency changes

pros.claim: hysteresis and tuning prevent oscillation
pros.example: a 2C deadband on a thermostat stops the heater relay from chattering near setpoint

cons.claim: poorly tuned loops oscillate or overshoot dangerously
cons.example: high PID gain on a heater overshoots and cycles the load destructively

acceptance_tests: loop has defined hysteresis/anti-windup and bounded output
stability verified across operating range
fail-safe output defined on sensor loss

nodes.definition: Define safe states, watchdogs, interlocks, and emergency stops so any fault, hang, or sensor loss drives the system to a non-harmful state.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any change to hazardous actuators, control logic, or the hazard analysis

pros.claim: watchdog + safe state contain firmware hangs
pros.example: a watchdog reset that de-energizes a heater relay prevents runaway on a crashed loop

cons.claim: fail-safes add cost/complexity that hobbyists skip
cons.example: omitting a watchdog lets a hung controller leave a pump running and flood a room

failure_modes: no safe state on sensor loss
acceptance_tests: every hazardous actuator has a defined safe state on fault/sensor-loss
watchdog and interlocks verified by fault injection
e-stop removes actuator power independent of firmware

nodes.definition: Select/design enclosures and environmental protection (IP rating, thermal, strain relief) appropriate to where the device physically lives.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the deployment environment or thermal/mechanical load changes

pros.claim: proper IP and strain relief prevent field failures
pros.example: an IP65 enclosure with glanded cable entries survives an outdoor sensor's rain exposure

cons.claim: over-engineered enclosures waste cost/space
cons.example: a sealed cast box on a desktop LED clock adds cost for no benefit

nodes.definition: Structure device firmware (event loop/RTOS tasks, non-blocking I/O, state machines) so sensing, control, and comms coexist without blocking.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new concurrent task or tighter timing deadline is introduced

pros.claim: non-blocking structure lets sensing and comms coexist
pros.example: a cooperative scheduler reads sensors while servicing MQTT without delay() stalls

cons.claim: blocking code starves time-critical tasks
cons.example: a blocking HTTP call delays a control loop past its deadline

nodes.definition: Provide over-the-air updates, versioning, and rollback so deployed devices can be patched without physical access while staying recoverable.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the device becomes physically inaccessible or the fleet requires remote patching

pros.claim: OTA + rollback keeps a fleet patchable and recoverable
pros.example: an A/B partition lets a bad update auto-revert instead of bricking a sealed device

cons.claim: OTA bugs can brick devices at scale
cons.example: an unverified update with a boot bug bricks every node simultaneously

failure_modes: update bricks device with no rollback

nodes.definition: Harden devices and links: secrets management, TLS/auth on broker and APIs, network segmentation, and least-privilege exposure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a device or broker becomes reachable beyond the trusted local segment

pros.claim: TLS+auth+segmentation limit blast radius
pros.example: a VLAN-isolated, auth-required broker stops a compromised bulb from reaching the LAN

cons.claim: security adds friction makers skip on home builds
cons.example: an anonymous-access MQTT broker exposed to the internet lets anyone actuate devices

acceptance_tests: broker/API require auth and TLS where exposed
IoT devices segmented from trusted LAN
no secrets committed to source

nodes.definition: Plan and execute reliable wiring/connectors/soldering with labeling and strain relief so the physical build matches the schematic and survives handling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: wire current ratings or connector/mechanical stresses change

pros.claim: good wiring practice makes builds reliable and serviceable
pros.example: ferruled, labeled wires in a terminal block let a fault be traced in seconds

cons.claim: rework on bad wiring is slow and error-prone
cons.example: unlabeled rats-nest wiring turns one sensor swap into hours of tracing

nodes.definition: Add logging, telemetry, and health metrics so device/automation behavior is diagnosable without physical probing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new fault class needs diagnosis or the fleet outgrows manual monitoring

pros.claim: telemetry makes intermittent field faults diagnosable
pros.example: a heartbeat + last-error topic reveals which node drops off at night

cons.claim: excess logging burdens constrained devices
cons.example: verbose per-loop logging floods a low-RAM MCU and slows the control loop

nodes.definition: Validate the build via bench tests, fault injection, and hardware-in-the-loop checks before deployment to confirm safe, correct behavior.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: control or safety-relevant logic changes and must be re-verified

pros.claim: fault injection proves fail-safes actually work
pros.example: pulling a sensor wire on the bench confirms the controller enters safe state

cons.claim: thorough testing slows hobby iteration
cons.example: writing HIL harnesses for a weekend project can exceed the build time

acceptance_tests: safety-critical behaviors verified by fault injection before deployment
each requirement has a passing acceptance test
regression suite re-run after changes

nodes.definition: Install, configure, and commission the system in its real location, verifying end-to-end behavior and handing off operating docs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the system is installed in a new site or operating conditions shift

pros.claim: commissioning catches site-specific faults bench tests miss
pros.example: on-site WiFi dead-spots and real loads surface only during commissioning

cons.claim: irreversible installs are costly to redo
cons.example: a sealed-in conduit run must be re-pulled if a wire was mis-sized

failure_modes: missing handoff docs strand the owner

nodes.definition: Plan ongoing maintenance, calibration drift handling, spares, and end-of-life so deployed automation stays reliable over time.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: telemetry indicates drift/wear or a component reaches end-of-life

pros.claim: scheduled calibration counters sensor drift
pros.example: annual recalibration keeps a CO sensor's safety threshold trustworthy

cons.claim: maintenance is easy to defer until failure
cons.example: an un-replaced backup battery dies and a power blip wipes the automation config

failure_modes: no decommission plan for hazardous loads

nodes.definition: Build the bill of materials, select sourceable parts, and balance cost vs availability/quality within the project budget.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a part becomes unavailable or a cost/quality target changes

pros.claim: a vetted BOM prevents counterfeit/unavailable-part stalls
pros.example: choosing a stocked, genuine sensor avoids a clone with a different I2C address

cons.claim: cheapest-part optimization risks quality/safety
cons.example: an uncertified clone power supply lacks the isolation the design assumed

revisit_triggers: quality issue traced to a part

edges.why_related: scope fixes the I/O, timing, and compute that platform choice must satisfy
edges.example: scope demanding hard-real-time PWM forces an MCU choice
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; re-pick platform if scope changes

edges.why_related: scope defines which parts the BOM must include
edges.example: adding outdoor sensing adds a weatherproof sensor line item

edges.why_related: power/fusing budget bounds what current a driver may switch
edges.example: the fused rail caps the motor driver's allowable stall current

edges.why_related: supply/reference and isolation decisions bound sensor wiring
edges.example: the SELV rail and reference set the analog sensor's usable range

edges.why_related: platform pinout and bus support constrain sensor interfacing
edges.risk_of_conflict: unsupported bus if platform fixed late
edges.example: an MCU lacking a free I2C bus blocks a planned sensor
edges.resolution_rule: platform capability dominates sensor bus choice

edges.why_related: platform PWM/GPIO and timing constrain actuator signaling
edges.risk_of_conflict: signal mismatch if platform fixed late
edges.example: lack of hardware PWM forces a different servo strategy

edges.why_related: platform (MCU vs Linux, RTOS vs loop) determines firmware structure
edges.example: an RTOS-capable MCU enables task-based firmware

edges.why_related: platform radios determine available connectivity
edges.example: a Pi has WiFi+BLE while a bare AVR has none
edges.resolution_rule: platform radio set dominates connectivity options

edges.why_related: sensor pinouts and levels define part of the wiring plan
edges.example: an I2C sensor's pull-up and bus wiring enter the harness

edges.why_related: driver current and connectors set wire gauge and connectorization
edges.example: a 5A motor lead requires heavier gauge and a rated connector

edges.why_related: validated actuator drive is required before motion coordination
edges.example: working stepper drive precedes differential-drive kinematics
edges.resolution_rule: drive layer dominates motion build order

edges.why_related: a working network/radio link is required before MQTT messaging
edges.example: WiFi must associate before the MQTT client can connect

edges.why_related: topic/payload design feeds hub entity discovery and modeling
edges.example: MQTT discovery topics auto-create Home Assistant entities
edges.resolution_rule: messaging design dominates hub entity model

edges.why_related: hub entities provide the state model rules trigger on
edges.example: an automation triggers off the hub's motion-sensor entity
edges.resolution_rule: hub entity model dominates rule authoring

edges.why_related: trustworthy sensor state is required for rule triggers
edges.example: a debounced door sensor feeds an arm/disarm rule
edges.resolution_rule: sensor validity dominates rule trigger trust

edges.why_related: rule actions must map to working actuator commands
edges.example: a 'lights on' action maps to the relay driver
edges.resolution_rule: drive layer dominates rule action set

edges.why_related: discrete rules precede and frame closed-loop control design
edges.example: an on/off rule becomes a hysteresis loop for a thermostat
edges.resolution_rule: establish rule semantics before closing the loop

edges.why_related: the control loop's behavior defines required safe states and interlocks
edges.example: a heater PID loop mandates a watchdog-driven safe-off state

edges.why_related: power topology defines how actuator energy is removed in a safe state
edges.example: an e-stop opens the actuator supply contactor independent of firmware

edges.why_related: firmware structure must host watchdogs and safe-state transitions
edges.example: a watchdog task in the firmware forces safe state on a stalled loop

edges.why_related: non-blocking firmware structure should exist before adding network I/O
edges.example: an event loop services WiFi without blocking sensor reads
edges.resolution_rule: structure firmware before bolting on connectivity

edges.why_related: firmware architecture must support update/rollback partitions
edges.example: A/B partitions in firmware enable rollback on a bad OTA

edges.why_related: a network link is required to deliver OTA updates
edges.example: the device pulls a signed image over WiFi

edges.why_related: the connectivity surface defines what must be secured
edges.benefit_of_coupling: security covers the real attack surface
edges.example: an internet-reachable broker mandates TLS and auth

edges.why_related: broker topics/commands define authz and encryption needs
edges.example: actuator-command topics require authenticated, encrypted access

edges.why_related: firmware hooks emit the logs/telemetry observability consumes
edges.example: firmware publishes a heartbeat and last-error to a telemetry topic

edges.why_related: the messaging layer transports telemetry to dashboards
edges.example: health topics flow over the same broker to a dashboard

edges.why_related: control behavior must be validated before deployment
edges.example: HIL tests confirm the loop is stable across the operating range
edges.resolution_rule: control must pass validation before lock

edges.why_related: safe states must be proven by fault injection
edges.example: yanking a sensor wire on the bench confirms safe-off
edges.resolution_rule: fail-safe must be validated before deployment

edges.why_related: rule behavior and interactions must be tested
edges.example: tests confirm two lighting rules don't race
edges.resolution_rule: rules must be validated before deployment

edges.why_related: validated, go/no-go results gate physical deployment
edges.example: a passing go/no-go report authorizes on-site install

edges.why_related: environmental protection must be ready before field install
edges.example: an IP-rated enclosure is fitted before an outdoor install

edges.why_related: commissioning hands off to ongoing maintenance
edges.example: the commissioning record seeds the maintenance schedule

edges.why_related: telemetry trends trigger maintenance actions
edges.example: rising error rates schedule a recalibration visit
edges.resolution_rule: stop when telemetry returns to baseline after maintenance

edges.why_related: selected connectors/wire/parts feed the assembly step
edges.example: the chosen terminal blocks and gauge define the harness build

edges.why_related: hardening (TLS/auth/segmentation) adds friction to easy connectivity
edges.example: TLS+auth on a broker complicates quick device onboarding
edges.resolution_rule: security dominates whenever a device is reachable beyond the trusted segment

edges.why_related: fail-safe interlocks can override or block convenient automation actions
edges.example: a safety interlock blocks an automation that would run a pump dry

edges.why_related: tight control loops demand timing that competes with other firmware tasks
edges.example: a 1kHz control loop competes with network servicing for CPU
edges.resolution_rule: control-loop deadlines dominate non-critical firmware tasks

edges.why_related: cheapest-part sourcing can undercut required safety margins
edges.example: a cheap clone PSU lacks the isolation the design assumed

edges.why_related: remote updates introduce a path to push unsafe firmware to live devices
edges.risk_of_conflict: fleet-wide unsafe state if convenience wins
edges.example: an unverified OTA could disable a watchdog across the fleet
edges.resolution_rule: fail-safe integrity dominates OTA convenience; updates must preserve safe states

conflict_axes.trigger: an automation or control action would violate a safe-state or interlock condition
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: safety interlocks and safe states always override convenience automation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: any hazardous actuator can be commanded into an unsafe state
conflict_axes.example: a 'fill the tank' automation is blocked by a high-level interlock to prevent overflow

conflict_axes.trigger: a device is exposed beyond the trusted local segment without auth/TLS
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: any path reachable beyond the trusted segment must be authenticated and encrypted before convenience
conflict_axes.example: an open MQTT broker is closed behind auth+TLS before remote dashboards are enabled

conflict_axes.trigger: a cheaper part undercuts a safety, isolation, or current-rating margin
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: safety/rating-critical parts must meet spec regardless of cost; only non-critical parts may be cost-optimized
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a cost-driven substitution touches a mains, isolation, or fusing part
conflict_axes.example: a certified isolated PSU is chosen over a cheaper clone for a mains-switching build

conflict_axes.trigger: network/feature tasks threaten the control loop's timing deadline
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: hard control-loop deadlines preempt non-critical firmware/network work
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: control loop misses deadlines under feature load
conflict_axes.example: network polling is moved off the critical path so a 1kHz loop keeps its deadline

conflict_axes.trigger: autonomous behavior conflicts with a human's manual override or e-stop
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: manual override and e-stop always win over autonomous rules
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: automation can re-enable a load a human just stopped
conflict_axes.example: an e-stop latches off a motor until a human resets it, ignoring the automation

conflict_axes.trigger: a remote update could push unverified firmware that weakens safety to many devices
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: updates must be validated, signed, staged, and reversible and must preserve safe states
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: an OTA can alter safety logic without staged rollout
conflict_axes.example: a safety-touching OTA is canaried on one device with rollback before fleet rollout

conflict_axes.trigger: robustness work (tests, telemetry, fail-safes) competes with a fast hobby build
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: robustness is mandatory wherever a hazard or irreversible action exists; optional elsewhere
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a hazardous or irreversible function is shipped without tests or fail-safe
conflict_axes.example: a non-hazardous LED clock skips HIL tests but a heater controller does not

conflict_axes.trigger: core automation is made to depend on an external/cloud link that can fail
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: safety-relevant and core control must work locally; cloud is for convenience only
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a safe-state or core loop depends on an internet link
conflict_axes.example: a thermostat keeps controlling locally when the internet/hub is down

edge_cases.trigger: a rule references a hub entity id that was renamed
edge_cases.example: renaming a sensor entity breaks every rule that triggered on it
edge_cases.detection_method: static check that every rule trigger resolves to an existing entity id
resolution: remap rule to current entity id

edge_cases.trigger: a hazardous control loop ships without a defined safe state on sensor loss
edge_cases.example: a heater PID keeps full power when its thermocouple disconnects
edge_cases.detection_method: fault-injection test pulling each sensor input and asserting safe state

edge_cases.trigger: an inductive load is driven without flyback/snubber
edge_cases.example: a relay coil without a diode spikes and kills the MOSFET over time
edge_cases.detection_method: design review checklist asserts every inductive load has protection

edge_cases.trigger: a blocking network call sits inside the control path
edge_cases.example: a blocking MQTT publish stalls a motor control loop
edge_cases.detection_method: timing instrumentation flags loop iterations exceeding the deadline
resolution: move comms off the critical path

edge_cases.trigger: an MQTT broker is exposed without auth/TLS
edge_cases.example: anyone on the internet can publish to an actuator command topic
edge_cases.detection_method: network scan/config audit asserts auth+TLS on any externally reachable port

edge_cases.trigger: an unverified OTA without rollback is pushed fleet-wide
edge_cases.example: a boot bug in a mass OTA bricks all sealed nodes at once
edge_cases.detection_method: release gate asserts signed image, A/B rollback, and canary before fleet rollout

edge_cases.trigger: two rules command the same actuator on overlapping conditions
edge_cases.example: a presence rule and a schedule rule fight over one light
edge_cases.detection_method: static analysis flags multiple rules writing one actuator without precedence
resolution: add integration test for the actuator

edge_cases.trigger: sensor calibration drifts beyond tolerance in service
edge_cases.failure_mode: control acts on wrong measured value
edge_cases.example: a drifting gas sensor crosses its safety threshold late
edge_cases.detection_method: telemetry compares readings against expected ranges and flags drift

edge_cases.trigger: control and rule logic are conflated into one unbounded work unit
edge_cases.failure_mode: the step cannot be validated or handed off in one session
edge_cases.example: a single blob mixes rule scheduling and PID tuning
edge_cases.detection_method: node review asserts each node maps to one bounded session with its own acceptance tests
resolution: split into rule node and control node

edge_cases.trigger: a bench-validated device is installed in a harsher environment
edge_cases.failure_mode: ingress or thermal failure in the field
edge_cases.example: an indoor-tested node fails outdoors after rain
edge_cases.detection_method: commissioning checklist verifies enclosure rating against the actual site

edge_cases.trigger: a heuristic score is mislabeled observed without any dataset
edge_cases.failure_mode: unsupported empirical claim leaks into the KB
edge_cases.example: a confidence value is tagged observed though no logs exist
edge_cases.detection_method: validator scans labels and rejects observed/experimentally_validated without data

workflow.objective: fix sense-decide-act requirements and a feasible BOM
acceptance_tests: every requirement has a measurable threshold and acceptance test
workflow.do_first_because: scope errors propagate into platform, safety, and every downstream choice

workflow.objective: establish power, fusing, isolation, and environmental safety envelope
entry_criteria: scope locked enough to know loads and environment
acceptance_tests: all mains paths fused and isolated from SELV
enclosure rating matches environment
workflow.do_first_because: safety is high-irreversibility and high-risk; it must bound every later electrical decision

workflow.objective: choose platform and firmware architecture matched to timing and I/O
acceptance_tests: platform meets I/O, timing, compute, and power needs
firmware is non-blocking
workflow.do_first_because: platform is high-coupling: it constrains sensors, actuators, connectivity, and firmware

workflow.objective: interface sensors and actuators and wire the build reliably
acceptance_tests: sensors calibrated and read correctly
every inductive load protected
wiring within ratings
exit_criteria: I/O layer validated on the bench
workflow.do_first_because: stable I/O is required before any rule or control logic can be trusted

workflow.objective: establish links, messaging, and the hub state model
acceptance_tests: robust reconnect verified
topic/QoS/LWT defined
hub entities resolve
exit_criteria: devices report state into a coherent hub model
workflow.do_first_because: the hub state model must exist before automations can reference entities

workflow.objective: author triggers/rules and close sensor-actuator feedback loops
entry_criteria: I/O validated and hub entities available
acceptance_tests: rules deterministic with precedence
loops have hysteresis/anti-windup and bounded output
exit_criteria: automation and control logic defined and individually testable
workflow.do_first_because: control and rule logic is the highest-coupling work and must precede safety hardening and tests

workflow.objective: define safe states, interlocks, watchdogs, and device/network hardening
entry_criteria: control logic and exposure surface known
acceptance_tests: every hazardous actuator has a safe state on fault
exposed paths require auth+TLS
exit_criteria: fail-safes and hardening designed and ready to validate
workflow.do_first_because: fail-safe and security are high-risk; they must be set before validation and deployment

workflow.objective: validate behavior by bench/fault-injection/HIL and add telemetry and update path
acceptance_tests: safety behaviors proven by fault injection
each requirement has a passing acceptance test

priority_rationale.notes: scope fixes all downstream sense-decide-act and platform choices
electrical safety bounds every later electrical decision
sourceable parts must be settled before assembly
platform constrains sensors, actuators, firmware, connectivity
firmware structure underlies I/O, comms, and fail-safe hooks
environmental protection must precede field install
trustworthy sensing precedes rules and control
working drive precedes motion, rules, and control
physical build realizes the I/O design
a link precedes messaging, OTA, and security
messaging design precedes the hub state model
hub entities are the substrate for automations
motion builds on validated drive where applicable
rules map state to action for many devices
closed loops are the riskiest, highest-coupling logic
safe states and interlocks gate validation and deployment
hardening must precede any external exposure
remote updatability designed before fleet deployment
telemetry enables diagnosis and maintenance triggers
validation gates deployment of safety-critical behavior
irreversible install follows passing validation
lifecycle care follows commissioning

dominance_rules.trigger: a safety risk competes with build speed
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates speed for any hazardous or irreversible function
dominance_rules.required_action: add the required fail-safe before shipping
dominance_rules.example: a heater build waits for a watchdog even though it delays the demo

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node lacks a met prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: dependency order dominates value order in sequencing
dominance_rules.example: the flashy automation waits until sensors are validated

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number lacks supporting evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: label as heuristic and keep observed fields at 0.0
dominance_rules.example: a confidence value stays heuristic because no logs exist

dominance_rules.trigger: a node is proposed for hard lock before tests pass
dominance_rules.rule: QA dominates locking; no hard lock before acceptance and fault-injection tests pass
dominance_rules.example: deployment is blocked until fault injection confirms safe-off

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or hazardous decision is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible/high-risk actions
dominance_rules.required_action: obtain human sign-off and a decision record
dominance_rules.example: fleet-wide OTA touching safety requires human approval

dominance_rules.trigger: schema stability competes with adding more content
dominance_rules.rule: schema stability dominates raw content volume
dominance_rules.example: node structure is frozen before adding more nodes

dominance_rules.trigger: core control is tempted to depend on a cloud link
dominance_rules.rule: local safe control dominates cloud convenience
dominance_rules.example: a thermostat controls locally when the internet is down

dominance_rules.trigger: a device is exposed beyond the trusted segment
dominance_rules.rule: security dominates ease of setup for any external exposure
dominance_rules.required_action: require auth+TLS and segmentation before exposure
dominance_rules.example: an internet-reachable broker must use auth+TLS first

dominance_rules.trigger: a cost cut touches a safety-rated part
dominance_rules.required_action: keep the rated part regardless of cheaper clones
dominance_rules.example: a certified isolated PSU is kept over a clone

dominance_rules.trigger: control timing competes with feature/network load
dominance_rules.rule: hard control-loop deadlines dominate non-critical firmware work
dominance_rules.required_action: move non-critical work off the control path
dominance_rules.example: network polling is deferred so the control loop keeps its deadline

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not lock platform before scope is settled
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: platform chosen while requirements still churn
anti_rework_rules.example: an 8-bit MCU is picked before a TLS requirement surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not finalize drivers before the power/safety envelope is set
anti_rework_rules.rationale: unbudgeted current/isolation forces driver and wiring rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a driver is sized before fusing/isolation is known
anti_rework_rules.example: a motor driver is chosen before the fused rail current is fixed

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not author rules/control before I/O is validated
anti_rework_rules.rationale: logic built on bad readings or no-op actions is wasted
anti_rework_rules.example: a thermostat rule is tuned before the thermistor is calibrated

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not write automations before hub entities exist
anti_rework_rules.rationale: rules referencing missing entities silently fail
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: rules reference entity ids not yet created
anti_rework_rules.example: an automation triggers off an entity the hub has not discovered

anti_rework_rules.rule: define control behavior before designing fail-safes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: fail-safe scope depends on actual control risks
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: safe states designed without knowing control behavior
anti_rework_rules.example: a watchdog action is set before the control loop exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not deploy before fail-safes are validated
anti_rework_rules.rationale: field safety failures are costly and dangerous
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: install begins before fault injection passes
anti_rework_rules.example: a pump controller is installed before safe-off is proven

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not hard-lock before validation and human review pass
anti_rework_rules.rationale: hard locks before QA hide unverified risk
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a node is hard-locked before tests run
anti_rework_rules.example: deployment is hard-locked only after the go decision

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not expose devices externally before hardening
anti_rework_rules.rationale: exposed unhardened devices are immediately attackable
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a broker is exposed before auth/TLS is set
anti_rework_rules.example: remote access is enabled before segmentation exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not field-install before environmental protection is ready
anti_rework_rules.rationale: ingress/thermal failures in the field force re-install
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a bare board is installed outdoors
anti_rework_rules.example: an unsealed node is mounted outside before an IP enclosure is fitted

anti_rework_rules.rule: do not push fleet OTAs before rollback and canary exist
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unverified mass update can brick or unsafe the whole fleet
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a fleet update lacks rollback or canary
anti_rework_rules.example: an OTA is pushed to all devices without a canary stage

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or test reports a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: kb_validator/metrics or HIL test returns fail
acceptance_tests: every failing check is captured with its json_path

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and dependency impact
action: score defects by risk_if_wrong and blast radius
acceptance_tests: safety/high-risk defects sorted first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue ordered and no high-risk defect unranked

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling or safety node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace edges and dependencies from the defect node
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the defect node are listed
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: a prioritized defect is ready to fix
iteration_protocol.detection: route defect to its repair owner subsystem
action: apply formula-script recompute or reference fix
acceptance_tests: the targeted check passes after repair
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no repairable defect remains in queue

acceptance_tests: previously failing checks now pass with no new failures

action: flag nodes crossing the revisit delta
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed for all changed nodes
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no node exceeds the posterior revisit delta

iteration_protocol.detection: detect change to an upstream of a soft/hard-locked node
acceptance_tests: affected locks are downgraded and queued for revalidation
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: all impacted nodes revalidated and re-locked

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible defect cannot be auto-repaired
iteration_protocol.detection: defect on a risk>=0.80 node persists after max repair attempts
acceptance_tests: a human decision record exists for the escalated defect
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: human sign-off recorded or defect resolved

expected_properties: a closed loop or rule maps sensor to actuator
PWR_SAFETY and FAILSAFE are high-risk with acceptance tests

test_cases.input_summary: many WiFi nodes via MQTT and a hub

version_increment_rules: any change to a hard-locked node increments the KB version
safety-relevant logic change requires version increment and revalidation
lock_downgrade_rules: changing an upstream dependency downgrades dependent locks to draft
a failed revalidation downgrades the affected node to draft
